text: A lot also fell to the tribe of Manasseh, since he was Joseph's firstborn. Machir, Manasseh's firstborn and the father of Gilead, received Gilead and Bashan, because he was a man of war.

The rest of the descendants of Manasseh received land by their clans: the sons of Abiezer, the sons of Helek, the sons of Asriel, the sons of Shechem, the sons of Hepher, and the sons of Shemida. These were the male descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph, by their clans.
Now Zelophehad son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, had no sons, only daughters. These are the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

They came before Eleazar the priest, before Joshua son of Nun, and before the leaders, and said, "The LORD commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our brothers." So, at the LORD's command, he gave them an inheritance among the brothers of their father.
Thus ten portions fell to Manasseh, besides the land of Gilead and Bashan beyond the Jordan,
because the daughters of Manasseh received an inheritance along with his sons. The land of Gilead belonged to the rest of Manasseh's descendants.
The border of Manasseh ran from Asher to Michmethath, which lies east of Shechem; then the border went south to the inhabitants of En-tappuah.
The land of Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, but Tappuah itself, on Manasseh's border, belonged to the sons of Ephraim.
Then the border went down to the Wadi Kanah. South of the wadi these towns belonged to Ephraim, among the towns of Manasseh; Manasseh's territory lay north of the wadi, and it ended at the sea.
The land to the south belonged to Ephraim and the land to the north to Manasseh, with the sea as its border. On the north they bordered Asher, and on the east Issachar.

Within Issachar and Asher, Manasseh also held Beth-shean with its villages, Ibleam with its villages, Dor and its villages, En-dor and its villages, Taanach and its villages, and Megiddo and its villages—the three heights.[^1]

[^1]: The meaning of the Hebrew phrase rendered "the three heights" is uncertain; it may refer to three hill districts or high regions associated with these towns.

versions.text: Within Issachar and Asher, Manasseh also held Beth-shean with its villages, Ibleam with its villages, the inhabitants of Dor with its villages, the inhabitants of En-dor with its villages, the inhabitants of Taanach with its villages, and the inhabitants of Megiddo with its villages—three regions in all.
versions.explanation: The repeated construction 'the inhabitants of X with its villages' is grammatically awkward (plural 'inhabitants' followed by 'its') and clogs the rhythm when read aloud. Naming the towns directly matches the parallel items earlier in the verse. The final phrase שלשת הנפת is obscure; 'the three heights' is a closer rendering than the interpretive 'three regions in all', and a footnote noting the uncertainty of the Hebrew would help.

versions.text: Within Issachar and Asher, Manasseh also held Beth-shean with its villages, Ibleam with its villages, Dor and its villages, En-dor and its villages, Taanach and its villages, and Megiddo and its villages—the three heights.
versions.explanation: The content of the verse is complete—all six towns with their dependent villages are present, and the omission of the repeated "the inhabitants of" was an intentional stylistic revision. However, the obscure phrase שלשת הנפת ("the three heights") remains unexplained for the reader; a brief footnote flagging the uncertainty of the Hebrew, as anticipated in the earlier revision note, would help without altering the text.

text: But the descendants of Manasseh could not take possession of these towns, for the Canaanites were determined to go on living in that land.

versions.text: But the descendants of Manasseh could not take possession of these towns, for the Canaanites managed to remain living in that land.
versions.explanation: The verb יואל conveys determination or persistence on the part of the Canaanites, not merely that they 'managed' to stay. 'Were determined' captures the sense better and reads well aloud.

text: When the Israelites grew stronger, they put the Canaanites to forced labor, but they did not drive them out completely.
The descendants of Joseph said to Joshua, "Why have you given us only one lot and one portion as our inheritance, when we are a numerous people, for the LORD has blessed us so richly until now?"

Joshua answered them, "If you are such a numerous people, go up into the forest and clear ground for yourselves there in the land of the Perizzites and the Rephaim, since the hill country of Ephraim is too cramped for you."

But the descendants of Joseph said, "The hill country is not enough for us, and all the Canaanites living in the valley country have iron chariots—both those in Beth-shean with its villages and those in the Valley of Jezreel."

versions.text: But the descendants of Joseph said, "The hill country is not enough for us, and all the Canaanites living in the lowland have iron chariots—both those in Beth-shean with its villages and those in the Valley of Jezreel."
versions.explanation: ארץ העמק is literally 'the land of the valley'; 'lowland' is normally used for a different Hebrew term (shephelah). 'Valley country' also connects naturally with 'the Valley of Jezreel' later in the same sentence.

text: Then Joshua said to the house of Joseph, to Ephraim and Manasseh, "You are a numerous people and you have great strength. You shall not have only one lot,

for the hill country shall be yours. Though it is forest, you will clear it, and it shall be yours to its farthest limits. You will drive out the Canaanites, even though they have iron chariots and are strong."
